instructions: Put the saffron in the white wine and set it aside.
Toast the almonds in a dry skillet over medium heat for 3 minutes, shaking the pan, until they're golden. Transfer them to a cutting board.
Peel 1 garlic clove and add it to the almonds with 2 tbsp of the parsley. Chop everything together until it's fine and crumbly, then transfer it to a small bowl. This is your picada.
Scrub the clams and mussels under cold water and pull any beards off the mussels. Cut the cod into 2-inch chunks. Pat the cod and shrimp dry and sprinkle them with 1/2 tsp of the salt.
Heat the olive oil in a large wide pot over medium-high heat. Add the prosciutto and cook for 2 minutes, until the edges crisp.
Chop the onion. Add it to the pot with the remaining 1/2 tsp salt and cook for 6 to 7 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft and golden at the edges.
Mince the remaining 3 garlic cloves. Add them with the smoked paprika and stir for 30 seconds, until it smells toasty.
Pour in the saffron wine and scrape up anything stuck to the bottom of the pot. Let it bubble for 2 minutes, until it's reduced by about half.
Add the crushed tomatoes and fish stock. Bring it to a boil, then turn the heat down to a steady simmer and cook for 10 minutes, until it's slightly thicker.
Stir in the picada and simmer for 2 minutes.
Add the cod and the clams, cover, and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the shrimp and the mussels, cover, and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, until the shrimp are pink and curled and the shells have opened. Throw out any that stay shut. The cod is done when it flakes.
Take the pot off the heat. Squeeze in the juice of the lemon and stir in 2 tbsp of the parsley.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a squeeze of lemon.
Ladle it into warm bowls. Serve with the crusty bread.
method_notes: The lead (Cup of Yum, Spanish seafood, 5 stars from 32 ratings) builds a saffron, tomato and paprika stew and finishes it with a picada of almonds, parsley and garlic loosened with lemon; Food Network and Julia Eats thicken with ground almonds earlier and add ham and rosemary. I followed the lead's picada but stirred it in before the seafood so it thickens the sauce, kept the ham from the other two, and used bought fish stock and no squid or crab so it fits a weeknight. Food Network and Julia Eats pages showed no rating, so they are not eligible as lead.
